content.introduction: The FOMC held a meeting on September 15-16, 2026, and voted unanimously to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System also voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90 percent and to increase the primary credit rate to 4.0 percent, both effective September 17, 2026. The FOMC indicated a considerable probability of at least another 25 basis points of policy firming by the end of the year, citing elevated inflation and a near full employment labor market. The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for October 27-28, 2026.
body: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System was held in the offices of the Board of Governors on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. and continued on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 9:00 a.m.1 also indicated that a considerable probability was placed on at least 25 basis points of policy firming by the end of the year. Participants generally emphasized that inflation remained elevated while the labor market appeared to be near full employment, with some signs of strengthening, and that economic activity was expanding at a solid pace. Implementation Note (Released September 16, 2026 at 2:00 p.m.)

Heading into theOctober 27–28, 2026 meeting, the confirmed starting point is the current target range of 3.75% – 4%. At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting, the FOMC voted 12–0 to raise the range by 25 basis points. The September 16 policy statement said inflation remained elevated and that the increase would support a timelier return to its 2% goal. That official record does not guarantee a hold, hike, or cut at the next meeting.

### What is known before the announcement [...] The eight scheduled 2026 FOMC meetings are January 27–28; March 17–18; April 28–29; June 16–17; July 28–29; September 15–16; October 27–28; and December 8–9. The March, June, September, and December meetings include the Summary of Economic Projections (SEP).
